content.text: The text combines several works. Young people leave Winton for school and celebrate a final picnic at Port Edward’s old fort, later returning by boat. Letters describe journeys to New Haven, New York, the Adirondacks, Whitehall, Washington, and college life. A tribute praises Augusta Larned’s motherly, spiritual character, followed by an epilogue honoring science and family. A children’s health text explains muscles, nerves, organs, food, alcohol, tobacco, breathing, circulation, skin, senses, warmth, and hygiene. Scott’s *Lady of the Lake* follows Fitz-James through the Highlands, his duel with Roderick Dhu, Douglas’s return to Stirling, and Ellen’s appeal at court. In *The Fair Maid of Perth*, Henry Smith visits Simon Glover’s house in Perth, defends it from intruders, courts Catharine, and joins citizens traveling to Kinfauns to seek the provost’s aid.
